title: Anyone can stop Pexi recognising new Plus buyers by asking the quota route about 120 made-up phones a minute, so a shopper who just paid still gets the paywall
evidence: Local throwaway server via app/test/security-harness.mjs, fake RevenueCat, requests carry cf-connecting-ip like the tunnel (probe: scratchpad abuse-probe.test.mjs, test P4). Buyer at 10/10: GET /api/identify?gtin=...&deviceId=buyer-device-0001-aaaa -> 402 {'error':'scan_limit','limit':10,'used':10}. Purchase lands at RevenueCat. Attacker: 130 x GET /api/quota?deviceId=flood-quota-<i>-zzzzzz with a fresh x-shin-device + x-shin-device-key each, one address 203.0.113.9: 130 x 200 in 763 ms, 119 RevenueCat lookups (the 120-a-minute ceiling, scan-quota.ts:57,337). Buyer right after paying, with x-shin-plus: 1: scan -> 402 scan_limit; /api/quota -> 200 {'limit':10,'remaining':0,'plus':false}. Same buyer 61 s later, no flood: scan -> 200 catalogue_hit. Cause: a fresh id binds its own key on its first request (device-key.ts:83-94), so provesDevice passes and every made-up id costs a lookup; over the ceiling the answer is the last known one (scan-quota.ts:343), which for a new buyer is 'not Plus'. Door allows 6,000 per 10 min per address (rate-limit.ts:149), so one address sustains it for about 10 hours a day. Organic version (assumed, not measured): every free scan of a keyed phone also asks RevenueCat once per 10 minutes (server.ts freeScanAddressRefusal -> isPlus), so about 1,200 phones active in the same 10 minutes reach the same ceiling with no attacker.
fix: Give lookups for phones that say they paid (x-shin-plus: 1) their own budget, with a per-network cap on hinted lookups for never-seen ids; stop spending lookups on devices that neither hint nor were ever Plus (answer 'not Plus' from cache). Longer term, RevenueCat webhooks into a server table so no lookup is on the scan path.

title: Every per-address limit (door, free scans, paid calls) counts a full IPv6 address, so one IPv6 connection rotating addresses has no limit at all
evidence: Local server, test P2: 400 barcode scans, each a fresh x-shin-device, from 400 addresses inside 2001:db8:10:1::/64 -> 400 answered, 0 refused (the per-address free-scan cap is 150 a day). Door test (scratchpad abuse-door.test.mjs, door set to 50 per 10 min): one IPv4 address 198.51.100.90 -> 50 x 200 then 429 {'error':'That is a lot of requests in a short time...','retryAfterSeconds':600}; 300 requests from 300 addresses in 2001:db8:99:1::/64 -> 300 x 200, 0 refused. Keys are 'ip:'+clientAddress (server.ts doorRefusal, freeScanAddressRefusal, paidCallRefusal); only the Claude network limiter uses networkOf (/64). A Linux host or VPS with a /64 can use any of 2^64 source addresses. Assumed, not checked: Cloudflare forwards IPv6 clients' real address in cf-connecting-ip for this zone (its default).
fix: Key every per-address limiter on networkOf() for IPv6 (/64 is one household or one server), keep IPv4 per address.

title: Free shoppers can get past 10 scans a week: a new phone id is a new week, 150 a day per IPv4 address, unlimited over IPv6, and the public web app does it with a private browser window
evidence: Local server, test P1, one address 198.51.100.30: device victimless-device-0001 at 10 -> 11th GET /api/identify?gtin=... 402 scan_limit; next request with x-shin-device: fresh-id-p1-0 (no key needed) -> 200 catalogue_hit with a price range; 150 answered scans from that one address before 402 (1,050 a week against Plus's 100). Over IPv6 no cap (previous line). Live, read-only: GET https://relay.anjiawenda.com/ -> 200 text/html 6294 bytes, the full app shell (the iOS app bundles its own copy: native/capacitor.config server.hostname localhost, sync-web.mjs writes SHIN_API_BASE), and the web id lives in localStorage (public/js/device.js:31), so a private window is a fresh 10. Already known as A3 (fix log 2026-11-16); what changed: the address cap went from 30 to 150 (R36, rate-limit.ts:173) and the IPv6 and web paths were not recorded. That the web app scans in a mobile browser is assumed (beta testers used it), not checked.
fix: Stop serving the app shell at the public hostname (serve /api only; the iOS app does not need it), and key the free-scan cap per IPv6 /64. The full fix is Apple App Attest or DeviceCheck so one phone cannot mint ids (option 2 in the fix log).
fix_cost: 30 minutes for the shell and the /64 key; App Attest 1 to 2 days; $0

title: One address can fill the Mac's disk in about two hours through the usage-event route, which takes 200 events per request for any made-up phone and has no disk check
evidence: Local server, test P7: 25 x POST /api/events/batch from one address 198.51.100.70, no device headers, body 793,902 bytes = 200 events {deviceId:'junk-<r>-<j>-yyyy',type:'scan_shown',payload:{p:3,900 x 'x'}} -> each 200 {'stored':200,'dropped':0,'received':200}; scans.db plus WAL grew 18,148,664 bytes (0.73 MB a request), 68 ms a request on this PC. Unbound ids with no header pass owns() (device-key.ts:136-139). No per-day event cap and no diskHasRoom on this route (server.ts /api/events/batch; diskHasRoom only guards shutter and shelf frames). Door per address: 6,000 per 10 min, 75,000 a day (rate-limit.ts:149-150) = up to about 54 GB a day from one address. Live /api/health (read-only): diskFreeGb 46.6. So about 106 minutes at the door rate, less with several addresses; the disk_low alarm fires at 10 GB free on a 30-minute probe with two failures before an email (watch.ts:140, BRIEF). The junk sits in scans.db, the store that also holds scans, device keys and the weekly counts, and is copied by every nightly backup on the same disk. While it runs the one Node thread is busy about 70 percent of the time.
fix: Accept events only for the request's own device (header must match, as other routes do), cap events per device and per address per day (for example 2,000), and refuse with 507 when diskHasRoom fails.

title: The 1,000-a-month Claude cap can still be used up by one person, from 4 IPv4 networks in a day or 11 IPv6 networks in under two minutes; every shopper then loses the Claude estimate until the month turns
evidence: Local server with the fake Claude, test P6: 1,155 GET /api/identify?text=<unique name>&deviceId=drain-<net>-<k>-xxxxx with x-shin-claude: 1, fresh id each, 105 addresses in each of 11 IPv6 /64s -> 999 Claude calls in 97,976 ms (local), cap reached (1,000 with the earlier probe). Then an honest shopper, new id, new address 192.0.2.200, 'Honest Shopper Oat Milk 1L' -> 200 with 0 Claude asks; /api/health claudeMonthlyCap {'reached':true,'refusedAsks':102}. Limits in force: device 12 per 10 min (minted ids skip it), network 100 per 10 min and 250 a day (server.ts claudeNetworkLimiter), address 90 per 10 min. IPv4: 250 a day per /24, so 4 /24s drain it in a day. Dollars stay small: names are cut at 160 characters (server.ts MAX_NAME_CHARS_TO_CLAUDE), so the month's worst bill is a few dollars (arithmetic from the v3 rates, not a bill). The cap now alarms loudly (A2 fix holds). What is new: the per-network fix does not stop a determined caller.
fix: A daily global ceiling of the remaining cap divided by the days left in the month, so a drain costs one day, not the month; count IPv6 at /48 for Claude asks.

title: The 429 counts R36 added and the RevenueCat ceiling count are never shown on the health page, so the attacks above are silent
evidence: grep over app/: limiterRefusals() (rate-limit.ts:59) and entitlementLookupHealth() (scan-quota.ts:196, which holds limiterRefusals for the RevenueCat ceiling) are called only by tests (rate-limit-shared.test.mjs:94, plus-lookup.test.mjs:83); server.ts never reads them. Live GET /api/health keys: ok, uptimeSeconds, ..., claudeMonthlyCap, watch, diskFreeGb, newestBackupAt, deployCheckerSeenAt, sourcesLoaded, claudeRecent, power: no limiter or RevenueCat-ceiling field. The watch reads only revenueCatHealth().failures (watch.ts:412), and a ceiling refusal is not a failure; the only trace is a console.warn at most once a minute (scan-quota.ts:341). R36's fix text ('add a daily 429 count to the health check') and commit a08e574 ('refusal counts') read as done.
fix: Put limiterRefusals() and entitlementLookupHealth() into the /api/health body and have the watch alarm when the RevenueCat ceiling refuses lookups or 429s jump.

title: The server's memory of RevenueCat answers is never trimmed, so every made-up phone id stays in memory until a restart
evidence: scan-quota.ts:150 entitlementCache is a Map with no deletion; :353 and :363 add one entry per looked-up id. Bounded by the 120-a-minute ceiling: up to about 172,800 entries a day, tens of MB (assumed size per entry), cleared by any restart or deploy.
fix: Drop entries past their expiry when the map passes 10,000, as hintRecheckAt already does (scan-quota.ts:331).

title: A faked Plus header does not unlock Plus or lift the weekly limit when RevenueCat is the judge
evidence: Local server, test P3: device plus-faker-0001-aaaa at 10/10 with its own key, GET /api/identify?gtin=... with x-shin-plus: 1 -> 402 scan_limit; GET /api/quota with x-shin-plus: 1 -> 200 {'plus':false,'remaining':0}; the header caused exactly 1 RevenueCat re-check (once a minute per device, scan-quota.ts:329). Production's mode (REVENUECAT_SECRET_KEY set, SHIN_PLUS_TRUST_CLIENT unset) not readable from outside: assumed, since the register says limits are on and the trust-client mode prints a startup warning.

title: No Claude call is made without the shopper's consent header; a script can send the header, which only spends the capped allowance above
evidence: Local server, test P5 (consent enforced): GET /api/identify?text=<unknown name> without x-shin-claude -> 200, 0 Claude calls; same with x-shin-claude: 1 -> 200 with a distribution verdict, 1 Claude call. server.ts claudeAllowed: anything but '1' is no.

title: One IPv4 address is stopped by the door limit and the free-scan address cap as designed
evidence: Door test: 51st request from 198.51.100.90 -> 429 retry-after 600 (limit lowered to 50 for the test). P1: the 151st free scan from 198.51.100.30 across fresh ids -> 402 scan_limit. The address is taken from cf-connecting-ip only on a loopback socket (rate-limit.ts:218-226), so a direct caller cannot forge it (A1 fix holds in code; the Mac's tunnel origin not checked).
